clips.title: The memory question
clips.text: A larger local AI model needs more memory than your laptop has available. What now?

clips.title: Two devices
clips.text: localhost.ai lets your laptop and phone share the work of running one model.

clips.title: The coordinator
clips.text: The laptop coordinates everything: storing the model, planning placement, and serving the chat.

clips.title: The phone worker
clips.text: Pair over your local network. Switch on sharing to start the phone’s bundled worker.

clips.title: Safe capacity
clips.text: The planner reserves operating-system headroom, and includes only workers it can reach and use.

clips.title: Laptop first
clips.text: It fills the laptop first, then sends only the remaining layers to the phone.

clips.title: The example split
clips.text: Here’s an example: twenty-five layers on the laptop, and three more on the phone.

clips.title: How a reply runs
clips.text: Each device holds its layers and their context memory. Intermediate data travels between them during chat.

clips.title: Start the laptop
clips.text: Let’s try the workflow. Start the laptop app, then press Control P to show the pairing code.

clips.title: Pair the phone
clips.text: On the phone, open Server, choose Pairing, and scan that code to connect to the coordinator.

clips.title: Choose a model
clips.text: Open Models and choose a GGUF. The library shows its size, quantization, and whether it’s installed.

clips.title: Share the phone
clips.text: In Server, enable Share this phone. The foreground notification gives you a Stop sharing control.

clips.title: Preview placement
clips.text: Preview the split at your chosen context size, and check each device’s estimated layer allocation.

clips.title: Load
clips.text: Load the model. Once it is ready, the Server screen shows Running and the active model.

clips.title: Ask
clips.text: Open Chat and send a question. The coordinator uses the loaded model across its assigned devices.

clips.title: The result
clips.text: The answer streams back. In laptop mode, prompts stay on your LAN: one model across your devices.
